title: Local perfect lifting from a lisse residue complex without finite coefficient hypotheses
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning that it has a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $J\subseteq A$ an ideal, and assume $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/J^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. On the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/J^n}$, using constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves and derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ be locally derived $JB_X$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. Suppose $M\otimes^L_{B_X}\underline{A/J}\simeq
u_X^*C$, where $
u_X$ is the étale/pro-étale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $C$ is a bounded étale $A/J$-complex. Assume each $H^q(C)$ is étale locally constant with finitely generated $A/J$-module values [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and that there are integers $a\leq b$ with $H^q(C\otimes^L_{\underline{A/J}}N)=0$ for every degree-zero étale $A/J$-module sheaf $N$ and every $q
otin[a,b]$. Derived tensors are [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Then there is a pro-étale covering $\{U_t	o X\}$ and, for each $t$, a bounded complex $P_t^ ullet$ of finite projective $A$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] such that $M|_{U_t}\simeq (B_X|_{U_t})\otimes_A P_t^ ullet$. The last expression is termwise extension of the constant complex. Neither $A/J$ nor $A/J^n$ is required to be finite as a set or perfect over $A$.

Bhatt–Scholze, literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf, Lemma 6.6.8 and the forward proof of Proposition 6.6.11; apply on the finitely many connected open components of affine Noetherian charts.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adic-residue-finite-local-models] to obtain the covering sieve. For a member U, work first over its supplied affine weakly contractible covering object V. This supplies a bounded finite-projective P, complete local objects T and L, their finite isomorphisms, and the restriction functor with its two object comparisons.

Apply [lem-sfb-adic-perfect-reduction-hom-ml] to the actual Hom tower. Every finite isomorphism remains invertible under the normalized successor transition because it is conjugated scalar extension. Inductively it gives a residue isomorphism from every level. Mathlib eventualRange identifies the stable image at zero. Lift its invertible element through the surjective stable-image tower using Types.surjective_π_app_zero_of_surjective_map. The resulting section has invertible residue; its higher components need not have been chosen invertible.

Lift this compatible section using [lem-sfb-adic-complete-hom-section-surjective]. Evaluation at zero identifies the reduction of the resulting morphism g:T -> L with the chosen invertible residue. Both objects are complete, so [lem-sfb-adic-complete-residue-conservative] makes g invertible.

Take the inverse isomorphism L -> T. Map it through the supplied restriction functor to U and compose with the two specified slice comparisons. This gives the exact completed constant P-model required by the original theorem on every member of the covering sieve.

split_report.blueprint: The first sentence of det-lem-integral-models-stacks invokes the integral criterion; this is its local lifting input below lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect, realizing Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.6.8 by the equivalent Stacks 09C6 route. The unit and chapter are unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Step 7 uses the stated epimorphism from degree-zero cohomology of the sequential derived limit to the limit of degree-zero cohomology sheaves. This is a generic pro-etale homological tool, not a replacement for the integral-model route.
Steps 5 and 8 use bounded complexes of flat modules being K-flat to compute the displayed tensors termwise. No local-lifting conclusion is taken from this generic tool.
The steps use K-flat scalar extension, preservation of coefficient triangles, and tensor reassociation; the unit does not restate this general ringed-site operation.
Steps 2 and 7 use termwise products representing derived products when countable products are exact, so restriction and the Roos construction have the asserted derived meaning.
Steps 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8 use the equivalence on complete objects and its compatible quotient and completion-unit comparisons; it is used for arbitrary Noetherian coefficients, exactly as stated.
Step 8 uses exactness of constant realization on the short exact sequence of coefficient modules; no assertion about completeness or local models is inferred from this generic tool.
Step 7 may equivalently construct the compatible sequence using the stated nonempty-limit theorem on the fibers of the stable-image systems; the proof also spells out their surjectivity.
Step 3 applies the generic site theorem to A/J^n and its nilpotent ideal J/J^n. It supplies lissity only; perfect constancy is supplied separately.
Step 4 uses the existence of affine covering objects weakly contractible in the full pro-etale site, needed for simultaneous constancy and exact evaluation.
Steps 6 and 7 use exact module-sheaf evaluation at the chosen covering object. This gives projective free sheaves and lifts the Milnor epimorphism on sections.
Steps 2, 5, 7 and 8 use functorial Roos derived limits and their exactness; the local-lifting compatibility argument remains in the present item.
Steps 2 and 3 use the canonical tensor comparison for restriction and geometric stalks to retain the quotient normalizations. No proper-base-change or finite-coefficient theorem is used.
Step 4 uses the generic algebraic inverse-limit theorem over the complete ring A for the normalized tower of perfect stalk complexes. It supplies no sheaf trivialization.
Step 5 uses completeness of bounded complexes whose terms are inverse limits of power-torsion sheaves, applied to the explicit idempotent summands defining B tensor P.
Steps 2 and 7 use exact countable products of modules over any pro-etale ring sheaf; this is the generic site input for the Roos and Milnor calculations.
Step 2 identifies the slice at an open chart with its own pro-etale site and preserves the coefficient sheaves. The proof writes out the restriction and product argument.
